drugs.name: Oseltamivir
drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug; blood and tissue esterases form the active carboxylate, which blocks neuraminidase so new virions clump on the cell surface (influenza A and B); renally secreted, so adjust for renal impairment
drugs.adverseEffects: Nausea and vomiting (taking it with food helps), headache, serious skin reactions; no metabolism-related drug interactions expected
drugs.use: Drug of choice for influenza treatment and prophylaxis at any age, outpatient or inpatient, and in pregnancy; start within 48 hours; twice daily for 5 days

drugs.name: Zanamivir
drugs.mechanism: Neuraminidase inhibitor inhaled as a dry powder; low systemic absorption (about 4-17%), minimal metabolism, no renal dose adjustment listed
drugs.adverseEffects: Bronchospasm in asthma or COPD (an inhaled powder that is not a bronchodilator); headache, sinusitis, dizziness, ear-nose-throat infections; oropharyngeal or facial edema
drugs.use: Outpatient influenza treatment from age 7 and prophylaxis from age 5 in someone who can manage an inhaler; not recommended with underlying airway disease

drugs.name: Peramivir
drugs.mechanism: Neuraminidase inhibitor given intravenously, a single dose for outpatients; excreted unchanged by the kidney (renal dose adjustment); half-life about 20 h
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperglycemia, diarrhea or constipation, serious skin and hypersensitivity reactions; give only where infusion reactions can be treated
drugs.use: Influenza in a patient who cannot take or absorb the oral first-line agent; treatment only, never prophylaxis
